title: The Nutcracker and the Mouse King

s.t: It was Christmas Eve at Clara's house.
s.fr: C’était la veille de Noël chez Clara.

s.t: Clara and her brother stood by a tree.
s.fr: Clara et son frère se tenaient près d’un arbre.

s.t: Clara's parents welcomed many guests into the house.
s.fr: Les parents de Clara accueillirent de nombreux invités dans la maison.

s.t: Many guests stood by the tree too.
s.fr: De nombreux invités se tenaient aussi près de l’arbre.

paras.summary: On Christmas Eve, Clara and her brother stand by the tree while Clara's parents welcome many guests into the house.

s.t: Clara's brother wanted to open his presents.
s.fr: Le frère de Clara voulait ouvrir ses cadeaux.

s.t: "Not yet," said Clara's mother, "we must wait for our guests."
s.fr: « Pas encore, » dit la mère de Clara, « nous devons attendre nos invités. »

s.t: Clara's brother did not want to wait.
s.fr: Le frère de Clara ne voulait pas attendre.

paras.summary: Clara's brother wants to open his presents, but his mother says they must wait for the guests, and he does not want to wait.

s.t: Clara opened the door.
s.fr: Clara ouvrit la porte.

s.t: Her godfather stood at the door with a box.
s.fr: Son parrain se tenait à la porte avec une boîte.

s.t: Her godfather was an old clockmaker.
s.fr: Son parrain était un vieux fabricant d’horloges.

s.t: He made wonderful toys.
s.fr: Il fabriquait de merveilleux jouets.

s.t: Clara took her godfather inside.
s.fr: Clara fit entrer son parrain.

s.t: "Come in and get warm," said Clara's mother.
s.fr: « Entrez et réchauffez-vous, » dit la mère de Clara.

paras.summary: Clara opens the door to her godfather, an old clockmaker who makes wonderful toys, standing there with a box, and she takes him inside, where her mother welcomes him.

s.t: Clara's brother looked at the box.
s.fr: Le frère de Clara regarda la boîte.

s.t: "What is inside the box?" he said.
s.fr: « Qu’est-ce qu’il y a dans la boîte ? » dit-il.

s.t: Clara wanted to see inside the box too.
s.fr: Clara voulait voir à l’intérieur de la boîte aussi.

s.t: "You must wait and see," said the old clockmaker.
s.fr: « Vous devez attendre et voir, » dit le vieux horloger.

paras.summary: Clara's brother asks what is inside the box, and Clara wants to see inside it too, but the old clockmaker tells them they must wait and see.

s.t: The old clockmaker opened his box.
s.fr: Le vieux horloger ouvrit sa boîte.

s.t: Inside the box were many small toys.
s.fr: À l’intérieur de la boîte se trouvaient de nombreux petits jouets.

s.t: Many guests looked at the wonderful toys.
s.fr: De nombreux invités regardèrent les merveilleux jouets.

s.t: The old clockmaker turned to Clara.
s.fr: Le vieux horloger se tourna vers Clara.

paras.summary: The old clockmaker opens his box of many small toys for the guests, then turns to Clara.

s.t: "I have a wonderful gift for you," he said.
s.fr: « J’ai un merveilleux cadeau pour vous, » dit-il.

s.t: He gave Clara a small wooden man.
s.fr: Il donna à Clara un petit homme en bois.

s.t: The small wooden man had a big jaw.
s.fr: Le petit homme en bois avait une grande mâchoire.

s.t: He wore a red coat.
s.fr: Il portait un manteau rouge.

s.t: "This is a nutcracker," said the old clockmaker.
s.fr: « C’est un casse-noisette, » dit le vieux horloger.

s.t: "He can crack nuts with his jaw," he said.
s.fr: « Il peut casser des noix avec sa mâchoire, » dit-il.

paras.summary: He gives her a small wooden man with a big jaw and a red coat, a nutcracker that can crack nuts with his jaw.

s.t: Clara took the nutcracker in her arms.
s.fr: Clara prit le casse-noisette dans ses bras.

s.t: She found a small nut in a bowl.
s.fr: Elle trouva une petite noix dans un bol.

s.t: Clara put the nut in the nutcracker's jaw.
s.fr: Clara plaça la noix dans la mâchoire du casse-noisette.

s.t: The nutcracker cracked the nut.
s.fr: Le casse-noisette cassa la noix.

paras.summary: Clara takes the nutcracker, finds a small nut in a bowl, puts it in his jaw, and the nutcracker cracks it.

s.t: "Be careful with his jaw," said the old clockmaker.
s.fr: « Faites attention à sa mâchoire, » dit le vieux horloger.

s.t: Clara laughed and held the nutcracker close.
s.fr: Clara rit et serra le casse-noisette contre elle.

s.t: But her brother wanted to hold the nutcracker too.
s.fr: Mais son frère voulait tenir le casse-noisette aussi.

paras.summary: The old clockmaker warns her to be careful with the jaw; Clara laughs and holds the nutcracker close, but her brother wants to hold it too.

s.t: Clara gave the nutcracker to her brother.
s.fr: Clara donna le casse-noisette à son frère.

s.t: "Be careful with him," said Clara.
s.fr: « Fais attention avec lui, » dit Clara.

s.t: He held the nutcracker in his arms.
s.fr: Il tenait le casse-noisette dans ses bras.

s.t: Her brother found a big nut in the bowl.
s.fr: Son frère trouva une grosse noix dans le bol.

s.t: The nut was too big for the jaw.
s.fr: La noix était trop grosse pour la mâchoire.

paras.summary: Clara gives the nutcracker to her brother and warns him to be careful, and he finds a big nut in the bowl, too big for the jaw.

s.t: "This nut is too hard for him," said Clara.
s.fr: « Cette noix est trop dure pour lui, » dit Clara.

s.t: But her brother put the nut in the jaw.
s.fr: Mais son frère mit la noix dans la mâchoire.

s.t: He pushed hard on the jaw.
s.fr: Il poussa fort sur la mâchoire.

s.t: The nutcracker's jaw broke.
s.fr: La mâchoire du casse-noisette se cassa.

paras.summary: Clara says the nut is too hard for him, but her brother forces it in and pushes hard, and the nutcracker's jaw breaks.

s.t: Clara cried and took the nutcracker back.
s.fr: Clara pleura et reprit le casse-noisette.

s.t: "You broke my nutcracker!" said Clara.
s.fr: « Tu as cassé mon casse-noisette ! » dit Clara.

s.t: "I am sorry," said her brother.
s.fr: « Je suis désolé, » dit son frère.

s.t: Clara's mother told him to be careful next time.
s.fr: La mère de Clara lui dit d’être prudent la prochaine fois.

paras.summary: Clara cries and takes the nutcracker back, her brother says he is sorry, and their mother tells him to be careful next time.

s.t: Clara found a ribbon.
s.fr: Clara trouva un ruban.

s.t: She wrapped it around the nutcracker's jaw.
s.fr: Elle enroula cela autour de la mâchoire du casse-noisette.

s.t: Clara put the nutcracker in a small wooden bed.
s.fr: Clara posa le casse-noisette dans un petit lit en bois.

s.t: When the guests went home, Clara's mother said it was time for bed.
s.fr: Quand les invités rentrèrent chez eux, la mère de Clara dit qu’il était l’heure de dormir.

s.t: Clara went to her room, but she looked back at him.
s.fr: Clara alla dans sa chambre, mais elle regarda en arrière vers lui.

paras.summary: Clara wraps a ribbon around the broken jaw, puts the nutcracker in a small wooden bed, and goes to her room when the guests leave, looking back at him.

s.t: Night came, and the house was dark.
s.fr: La nuit tomba, et la maison était sombre.

s.t: Clara's parents and her brother were in bed.
s.fr: Les parents de Clara et son frère étaient au lit.

s.t: But Clara could not sleep at all.
s.fr: Mais Clara ne pouvait pas dormir du tout.

s.t: She wanted to look at the nutcracker's broken jaw.
s.fr: Elle voulait regarder la mâchoire cassée du casse-noisette.

s.t: Clara went down to the tree in the dark.
s.fr: Clara descendit jusqu’à l’arbre dans l’obscurité.

s.t: She found him in his small bed.
s.fr: Elle le trouva dans son petit lit.

paras.summary: Night comes and the house is dark, with everyone in bed, but Clara cannot sleep, so she goes down to the tree in the dark and finds the nutcracker in his small bed.

s.t: A clock struck midnight.
s.fr: Une horloge sonna minuit.

s.t: Mice came from under the floor and the door.
s.fr: Des souris vinrent de sous le plancher et la porte.

s.t: The floor was dark with mice.
s.fr: Le plancher était sombre de souris.

s.t: One mouse had a small crown.
s.fr: Une souris avait une petite couronne.

s.t: He was the mouse king.
s.fr: Il était le roi des souris.

paras.summary: A clock strikes midnight, and mice come from under the floor and the door until the floor is dark with them, and one mouse with a small crown is the mouse king.

s.t: The mouse king came behind his mice.
s.fr: Le roi des souris vint derrière ses souris.

s.t: Clara went behind a chair in the dark.
s.fr: Clara alla derrière une chaise dans l’obscurité.

paras.summary: The mouse king comes behind his mice, and Clara goes behind a chair in the dark.

s.t: The nutcracker grew as big as Clara.
s.fr: Le casse-noisette devint aussi grand que Clara.

s.t: His small bed fell to the floor.
s.fr: Son petit lit tomba sur le plancher.

s.t: The ribbon was still on his broken jaw.
s.fr: Le ruban était encore sur sa mâchoire cassée.

s.t: All the mice grew big too.
s.fr: Toutes les souris devinrent grandes aussi.

s.t: The nutcracker stood up.
s.fr: Le casse-noisette se leva.

paras.summary: The nutcracker grows as big as Clara, his small bed falls to the floor, the ribbon still on his broken jaw; all the mice grow big too, and the nutcracker stands up.

s.t: Clara still wore her slippers.
s.fr: Clara portait encore ses chaussons.

s.t: The toy soldiers stood by the tree.
s.fr: Les soldats jouets se tenaient près de l’arbre.

s.t: They had grown big too.
s.fr: Eux aussi, ils avaient grandi.

s.t: "Here come the mice!" said the nutcracker.
s.fr: « Voilà les souris ! » dit le casse-noisette.

paras.summary: Clara still wears her slippers, and the toy soldiers by the tree have grown big too, as the nutcracker calls out that the mice are coming.

s.t: The mice ran at the soldiers.
s.fr: Les souris coururent vers les soldats.

s.t: The wooden soldiers fell down hard.
s.fr: Les soldats de bois tombèrent durement.

s.t: Many mice fell down too.
s.fr: Beaucoup de souris tombèrent aussi.

s.t: The mice ran away.
s.fr: Les souris s’enfuirent.

paras.summary: The mice run at the soldiers; the wooden soldiers fall down hard, many mice fall down too, and the mice run away.

s.t: The mouse king did not run.
s.fr: Le roi des souris ne courut pas.

s.t: He fought the nutcracker.
s.fr: Il combattit le casse-noisette.

s.t: The mouse king pushed him back.
s.fr: Le roi des souris le repoussa.

s.t: The nutcracker fell to the floor.
s.fr: Le casse-noisette tomba par terre.

paras.summary: But the mouse king does not run: he fights the nutcracker, pushes him back, and the nutcracker falls to the floor.

s.t: Clara watched from behind the chair.
s.fr: Clara observa depuis derrière la chaise.

s.t: The mouse king stood over the nutcracker.
s.fr: Le roi des souris se tint au-dessus du casse-noisette.

s.t: The nutcracker could not get up.
s.fr: Le casse-noisette ne pouvait pas se lever.

s.t: Clara was afraid for him.
s.fr: Clara avait peur pour lui.

paras.summary: Clara watches from behind the chair as the mouse king stands over the nutcracker, who cannot get up, and she is afraid for him.

s.t: Clara ran to the nutcracker.
s.fr: Clara courut vers le casse-noisette.

s.t: She looked down at her slippers.
s.fr: Elle regarda ses chaussons.

s.t: Clara took off one slipper.
s.fr: Clara enleva un chausson.

s.t: She threw the slipper at the mouse king.
s.fr: Elle lança le chausson au roi des souris.

s.t: The slipper struck the mouse king.
s.fr: Le chausson frappa le roi des souris.

s.t: The mouse king fell down.
s.fr: Le roi des souris tomba.

paras.summary: Clara runs to the nutcracker, looks down at her slippers, takes one off, and throws it at the mouse king, and it hits him, and he falls down.

s.t: All the mice ran away.
s.fr: Toutes les souris s’enfuirent.

s.t: The mouse king ran away too.
s.fr: Le roi des souris s’enfuit aussi.

s.t: The nutcracker stood.
s.fr: Le casse-noisette se leva.

s.t: Clara was not afraid now.
s.fr: Clara n’avait plus peur maintenant.

s.t: He looked at Clara.
s.fr: Il regarda Clara.

s.t: The soldiers went back to the tree.
s.fr: Les soldats retournèrent à l’arbre.

paras.summary: All the mice run away, and the mouse king runs away too, so the nutcracker stands, and Clara is not afraid now; he looks at Clara, and the soldiers go back to the tree.

s.t: Then the nutcracker turned into a young man.
s.fr: Puis le casse-noisette se transforma en jeune homme.

s.t: He still wore his red coat.
s.fr: Il portait encore son manteau rouge.

s.t: "Thank you for saving me," he said.
s.fr: « Merci de m’avoir sauvé, » dit-il.

s.t: The young man had kind eyes.
s.fr: Le jeune homme avait des yeux doux.

s.t: She said nothing.
s.fr: Elle ne dit rien.

s.t: He said he had a story to tell.
s.fr: Il dit qu’il avait une histoire à raconter.

paras.summary: Then the nutcracker turns into a young man, still wearing his red coat, and he thanks Clara for saving him; the young man has kind eyes, and she says nothing, so he tells her he has a story to tell.

s.t: The young man told Clara a story.
s.fr: Le jeune homme raconta une histoire à Clara.

s.t: "My uncle is your godfather," he said.
s.fr: « Mon oncle est votre parrain, » dit-il.

s.t: "A king had a beautiful princess."
s.fr: « Un roi avait une belle princesse. »

paras.summary: The young man tells Clara a story: his uncle is her godfather, he says, and a king had a beautiful princess.

s.t: "One night, mice ate the king's cake."
s.fr: « Une nuit, des souris mangèrent le gâteau du roi. »

s.t: "The king killed the mouse queen's mice."
s.fr: « Le roi tua les souris de la reine des souris. »

s.t: "The mouse queen swore revenge on the king."
s.fr: « La reine des souris jura vengeance contre le roi. »

s.t: "She cursed the princess to be ugly."
s.fr: « Elle maudit la princesse à être laide. »

s.t: "But a hard nut could break the curse."
s.fr: « Mais une noisette dure pouvait briser la malédiction. »

paras.summary: One night mice ate the king's cake, so the king killed the mouse queen's mice, and the mouse queen swore revenge on the king and cursed the princess to be ugly, but a hard nut could break the curse.

s.t: "My uncle took me to the princess to crack it."
s.fr: « Mon oncle m’emmena chez la princesse pour la casser. »

s.t: "I cracked the hard nut and gave it to the princess."
s.fr: « Je cassai la noisette dure et la donnai à la princesse. »

s.t: "The princess ate it and was beautiful again."
s.fr: « La princesse la mangea et fut de nouveau belle. »

paras.summary: His uncle took him to the princess to crack it, and he cracked the nut and gave it to the princess, and she ate it and was beautiful again.

s.t: "But I had to step back, and I stepped on the mouse queen."
s.fr: « Mais je dus reculer et je marchai sur la reine des souris. »

s.t: "The mouse queen died and cursed me."
s.fr: « La reine des souris mourut et me maudit. »

s.t: "I turned into a small nutcracker with a big jaw."
s.fr: « Je me transformai en un petit casse-noisette avec une grande mâchoire. »

s.t: "My uncle could not break the curse."
s.fr: « Mon oncle ne put pas briser la malédiction. »

paras.summary: But he had to step back and stepped on the mouse queen, who died and cursed him, so he turned into a small nutcracker with a big jaw, and his uncle could not break the curse.

s.t: "Her son, the young mouse king, swore revenge on me."
s.fr: « Son fils, le jeune roi des souris, jura vengeance contre moi. »

s.t: "His mice came for me at midnight."
s.fr: « Ses souris sont venues me chercher à minuit ».

s.t: "But you broke the curse," said the young man.
s.fr: « Mais vous avez brisé le sortilège, » dit le jeune homme.

paras.summary: Her son, the young mouse king, swore revenge on him, and his mice came for him at midnight, but Clara, he says, broke the curse.

s.t: The young man held out his hand to Clara.
s.fr: Le jeune homme tendit la main à Clara.

s.t: "Come and see my home," he said.
s.fr: « Venez voir ma maison, » dit-il.

s.t: Clara wanted to see his home.
s.fr: Clara voulait voir sa maison.

s.t: The toy soldiers were small again by the tree.
s.fr: Les soldats de jouet étaient de nouveau petits près de l’arbre.

s.t: He took her to a coat on a hook.
s.fr: Il la conduisit vers un manteau sur un crochet.

paras.summary: The young man holds out his hand and asks Clara to come and see his home, and she wants to see it; the toy soldiers are small again by the tree as he takes her to a coat on a hook.

s.t: "Climb into the sleeve," said the young man.
s.fr: « Grimpez dans la manche, » dit le jeune homme.

s.t: Clara climbed into the sleeve.
s.fr: Clara grimpa dans la manche.

s.t: He climbed in too.
s.fr: Il grimpa aussi.

s.t: Clara could not see him in the dark.
s.fr: Clara ne pouvait pas le voir dans l’obscurité.

s.t: She held his hand and did not look back.
s.fr: Elle tint sa main et ne regarda pas en arrière.

paras.summary: He tells her to climb into the sleeve, and Clara climbs in, and he climbs in too; she cannot see him in the dark, so she holds his hand and does not look back.

s.t: The sleeve turned into a passage.
s.fr: La manche se transforma en un passage.

s.t: They went down and down the passage.
s.fr: Ils descendirent encore et encore dans le passage.

s.t: The passage grew warm.
s.fr: Le passage devint chaud.

paras.summary: The sleeve turns into a passage, and they go down and down the passage, which grows warm.

s.t: Clara saw a light.
s.fr: Clara vit une lumière.

s.t: The light came from a doorway.
s.fr: La lumière venait d’une porte.

s.t: The doorway was made of candy.
s.fr: La porte était faite de bonbons.

s.t: The young man smiled, and Clara smiled back.
s.fr: Le jeune homme sourit, et Clara lui sourit en retour.

s.t: Beyond the doorway was the candy kingdom.
s.fr: Au-delà de la porte se trouvait le royaume des bonbons.

paras.summary: Clara sees a light coming from a doorway made of candy, and the young man smiles at her and she smiles back, for beyond the doorway is the candy kingdom.

s.t: Clara and the young man went through the doorway.
s.fr: Clara et le jeune homme passèrent par la porte.

s.t: They stood still in the candy kingdom.
s.fr: Ils restèrent immobiles dans le royaume des bonbons.

s.t: Trees of chocolate grew all around them.
s.fr: Des arbres de chocolat poussaient tout autour d’eux.

s.t: A river of cream ran by the trees.
s.fr: Une rivière de crème coulait près des arbres.

s.t: They went by the river.
s.fr: Ils allèrent le long de la rivière.

s.t: Clara took a chocolate from a tree and ate it.
s.fr: Clara prit un chocolat d’un arbre et le mangea.

paras.summary: Clara and the young man go through the doorway and stand still in the candy kingdom, where trees of chocolate grow all around them; they go by a river of cream, and Clara takes a chocolate from a tree and eats it.

s.t: This kingdom was the young man's home.
s.fr: Ce royaume était la maison du jeune homme.

s.t: He was glad to be back.
s.fr: Il était content d’être de retour.

s.t: He still knew every tree by the river.
s.fr: Il connaissait encore chaque arbre le long de la rivière.

paras.summary: This kingdom is the young man's home, and he is glad to be back, for he still knows every tree by the river.

s.t: They saw a great palace.
s.fr: Ils virent un grand palais.

s.t: The palace was made of cookies and cake.
s.fr: Le palais était fait de biscuits et de gâteau.

s.t: Clara wanted to look inside.
s.fr: Clara voulait regarder à l’intérieur.

paras.summary: They see a great palace made of cookies and cake, and Clara wants to look inside.

s.t: They went to the palace.
s.fr: Ils allèrent au palais.

s.t: "This palace is wonderful," said Clara.
s.fr: « Ce palais est merveilleux, » dit Clara.

s.t: The young man smiled at her.
s.fr: Le jeune homme lui sourit.

paras.summary: They go to the palace, and Clara says it is wonderful, so the young man smiles at her.

s.t: Clara and the young man went into the palace.
s.fr: Clara et le jeune homme entrèrent dans le palais.

s.t: Many people stood inside.
s.fr: Beaucoup de gens se tenaient à l’intérieur.

s.t: Music played through the palace.
s.fr: De la musique jouait dans tout le palais.

s.t: The people welcomed Clara and the young man.
s.fr: Les gens accueillirent Clara et le jeune homme.

paras.summary: Clara and the young man go into the palace, where many people stand inside, music plays, and the people welcome them.

s.t: They made a great feast for them.
s.fr: Ils préparèrent un grand festin pour eux.

s.t: The feast had fruit, cookies, and cake.
s.fr: Le festin avait des fruits, des biscuits et du gâteau.

s.t: Clara ate the fruit and the cookies.
s.fr: Clara mangea les fruits et les biscuits.

paras.summary: They make a great feast with fruit, cookies, and cake, and Clara eats the fruit and the cookies.

s.t: "Thank you all," said the young man.
s.fr: « Merci à tous », dit le jeune homme.

s.t: "Clara saved us from the mouse king," he said.
s.fr: « Clara nous a sauvés du roi des souris », dit-il.

s.t: The people were glad for Clara.
s.fr: Les gens étaient contents pour Clara.

paras.summary: The young man thanks the people and says Clara saved them from the mouse king, and the people are glad for Clara.

s.t: Many people danced.
s.fr: Beaucoup de gens dansèrent.

s.t: The young man danced with Clara.
s.fr: Le jeune homme dansa avec Clara.

s.t: Clara smiled at the people.
s.fr: Clara sourit aux gens.

s.t: The feast went on all night.
s.fr: Le festin dura toute la nuit.

s.t: But Clara grew tired.
s.fr: Mais Clara devint fatiguée.

s.t: She wanted to go home now.
s.fr: Elle voulait rentrer chez elle maintenant.

paras.summary: Many people dance, and the young man dances with Clara, who smiles at the people; the feast goes on all night, but Clara grows tired and wants to go home now.

s.t: "It is time to go home," said the young man.
s.fr: « Il est temps de rentrer », dit le jeune homme.

s.t: Clara was too tired to go far.
s.fr: Clara était trop fatiguée pour aller loin.

s.t: The young man took her back to the doorway.
s.fr: Le jeune homme la ramena jusqu’à l’entrée.

paras.summary: The young man says it is time to go home, for Clara is too tired to go far, so he takes her back to the doorway.

s.t: They went into the passage again.
s.fr: Ils entrèrent de nouveau dans le passage.

s.t: The candy doorway closed behind them.
s.fr: L’entrée de bonbons se ferma derrière eux.

s.t: The passage was dark now.
s.fr: Le passage était sombre maintenant.

s.t: His red coat was warm in the dark.
s.fr: Son manteau rouge était chaud dans l’obscurité.

s.t: Clara held the young man's hand.
s.fr: Clara tint la main du jeune homme.

s.t: Her eyes grew heavy.
s.fr: Ses yeux devinrent lourds.

s.t: She could not hold them open.
s.fr: Elle ne pouvait pas les garder ouverts.

paras.summary: They go into the passage again, and the candy doorway closes behind them, so the passage is dark now, but his red coat is warm in the dark, and Clara holds the young man's hand as her eyes grow heavy, and she cannot hold them open.

s.t: The passage turned into the sleeve again.
s.fr: Le passage se transforma en manche de nouveau.

s.t: Clara was sleepy.
s.fr: Clara avait sommeil.

s.t: She closed her eyes.
s.fr: Elle ferma les yeux.

s.t: Clara did not remember climbing out.
s.fr: Clara ne se rappelait pas être sortie.

s.t: The young man's voice grew far away.
s.fr: La voix du jeune homme s’éloigna.

s.t: It grew quiet around her.
s.fr: Le silence se fit autour d’elle.

s.t: It grew dark.
s.fr: Il fit sombre.

paras.summary: The passage turns into the sleeve again, and Clara is sleepy and closes her eyes, not remembering climbing out, as the young man's voice grows far away, and it grows quiet around her and dark.

s.t: Clara woke on Christmas morning.
s.fr: Clara se réveilla le matin de Noël.

s.t: She was under the tree.
s.fr: Elle était sous l’arbre.

s.t: Clara held the small nutcracker in her arms.
s.fr: Clara tenait le petit casse-noisette dans ses bras.

s.t: His jaw was not broken now.
s.fr: Sa mâchoire n’était plus cassée maintenant.

s.t: Clara smiled at him.
s.fr: Clara sourit à lui.

paras.summary: Clara wakes on Christmas morning under the tree, holding the small nutcracker in her arms, his jaw not broken now, and she smiles at him.

s.t: Her brother found her by the tree.
s.fr: Son frère la trouva près de l’arbre.

s.t: "You slept under the tree!" said her brother.
s.fr: « Tu as dormi sous l’arbre ! » dit son frère.

s.t: Clara's mother came to see her too.
s.fr: La mère de Clara vint la voir aussi.

s.t: "I am home," said Clara.
s.fr: « Je suis chez moi, » dit Clara.

paras.summary: Her brother finds her by the tree and says she slept under it, and Clara's mother comes to see her too, so Clara says she is home.

s.t: She held up the small nutcracker.
s.fr: Elle leva le petit casse-noisette.

s.t: "He saved me," said Clara.
s.fr: « Il m’a sauvée, » dit Clara.

s.t: Her mother did not understand.
s.fr: Sa mère ne comprit pas.

s.t: But she smiled at Clara.
s.fr: Mais elle sourit à Clara.

paras.summary: She holds up the small nutcracker and says he saved her, but her mother does not understand, though she smiles at Clara.

s.t: Clara's old godfather came to see them.
s.fr: Le vieux parrain de Clara vint les voir.

s.t: He looked at the small nutcracker and smiled.
s.fr: Il regarda le petit casse-noisette et sourit.

s.t: "I gave you a wonderful gift," he said.
s.fr: « Je vous ai donné un cadeau merveilleux, » dit-il.

s.t: Clara smiled at her godfather.
s.fr: Clara sourit à son parrain.

paras.summary: Clara's old godfather comes to see them, looks at the small nutcracker and smiles, and says he gave her a wonderful gift, so Clara smiles at her godfather.

s.t: That day, the old clockmaker came back.
s.fr: Ce jour-là, le vieux horloger revint.

s.t: His young nephew came with him.
s.fr: Son jeune neveu vint avec lui.

s.t: They stood at the door.
s.fr: Ils se tenaient à la porte.

s.t: "Come in and get warm," said Clara's mother.
s.fr: « Entrez et réchauffez-vous, » dit la mère de Clara.

s.t: Clara's brother liked the young nephew.
s.fr: Le frère de Clara aimait le jeune neveu.

paras.summary: That day, the old clockmaker comes back, and his young nephew comes with him; they stand at the door until Clara's mother welcomes them in, and Clara's brother likes the young nephew.

s.t: Clara looked at the nephew.
s.fr: Clara regarda le neveu.

s.t: He bowed to Clara.
s.fr: Il s’inclina devant Clara.

s.t: His eyes were kind.
s.fr: Ses yeux étaient doux.

s.t: The nephew smiled at Clara.
s.fr: Le neveu sourit à Clara.

s.t: Clara knew that smile from somewhere.
s.fr: Clara connaissait ce sourire de quelque part.

s.t: It looked like the young man's from that night.
s.fr: Il ressemblait à celui du jeune homme de cette nuit-là.

paras.summary: Clara looks at the nephew, and he bows to her, his eyes kind, and smiles at her; she knows that smile from somewhere, for it looks like the young man's from that night.

s.t: She held her small nutcracker close.
s.fr: Elle serra son petit casse-noisette contre elle.

s.t: He looked at the nutcracker in her arms.
s.fr: Il regarda le casse-noisette dans ses bras.

s.t: "A fine nutcracker," he said.
s.fr: « Un beau casse-noisette, » dit-il.

paras.summary: She holds her small nutcracker close, and the nephew looks at it in her arms, calling it a fine nutcracker.

s.t: Clara smiled and said nothing.
s.fr: Clara sourit et ne dit rien.

s.t: The old clockmaker watched them.
s.fr: Le vieux horloger les observa.

s.t: Somewhere a clock struck in the quiet house.
s.fr: Quelque part une horloge sonna dans la maison silencieuse.

paras.summary: Clara smiles and says nothing, the old clockmaker watches them, and somewhere a clock strikes in the quiet house.
